rationale: The claim accurately summarizes the findings and explicit limitations reported in the source study (S-EVID-007). The study explicitly states a "small positive correlation" between neuron coverage and steering angle deviation (S-EVID-007-R1), clarifies "we do not know that the increase in neuron coverage is causing the increase" (S-EVID-007-R1), and concludes that "there is a need for further investigation to discover whether neuron coverage is a consistent indicator" (S-EVID-007-R2). These statements directly support all parts of the claim. The scope of the claim ("One DNN and transformed-image test study; no demonstrated safety-failure threshold") is also directly confirmed by the study's "Threats to Validity" section (S-EVID-007-R1). No alternative interpretation, primary counterevidence, scope limit, or current-status change within the provided material defeats the claim as stated.
evidence_locators: S-EVID-007-R1: PDF pp. 7-8, excerpt: "Based on our data, we see a small positive correlation...", "However, care must be taken with this correlation as we do not know that the increase in neuron coverage is causing the increase...", "Our experiments and results have some limitations. We have worked with only one DNN model...", "Another limitation of our analysis is that it does not isolate when the SAD rises to the level of grossly erroneous or failure inducing."
S-EVID-007-R2: PDF p. 8, excerpt: "there is a need for further investigation to discover whether neuron coverage is a consistent indicator"
limitations: Review limited to supplied evidence packet; no external search performed.
